rationale: The book's cited texts define righteousness in exactly the terms the book claims: Deuteronomy 6:25 is an explicit scriptural definition ('it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments'), Psalm 119:172 equates the commandments with righteousness, and 1 John 3:7 — framed as a warning against deception — states that the one who does righteousness is righteous. The proving chapter then vindicates the garment elaboration from Revelation 19:8's own interpretive key (the fine linen is the dikaiomata, plural righteous acts, of the saints), a lexical fact the common 'imputed status' reading must flatten via the KJV's singular rendering. The strongest counter — forensic/imputed righteousness as a received legal status — cannot account for the supplied texts that make righteousness something done, kept, defiled by conduct, and washed (Rev 3:4; 16:15; Zech 3:4; Job 29:14; Rev 22:14) without recasting them as metaphor for something else. Meanwhile the book absorbs the counter's best evidence within the supplied case: the linen 'was given unto her' (grace-grounded, Eph 2:10), Isaiah 64:6 is answered by reading the whole verse (the doer's uncleanness stains the deed, not the deed itself), and Genesis 15:6 harmonizes under the accepted prior findings that faith and belief are themselves constituted by obedient response. Under established premises (love = keeping the commandments; faith/belief as obedient trust), the book's identification is the coherent completion of an already-adjudicated vocabulary. The comparative inference favors the book across the actual evidence.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments — righteous acts performed (the law kept) — not a vague moral goodness and not merely a forensic verdict received; symbolically, it is the fabric of the wedding garment, righteousness enacted and worn.
book_secondary_elaborations: The garment/fine-linen imagery: righteous acts woven, worn, kept clean, and washable (Rev 19:8; Isa 61:10; Rev 3:4; 7:14)
The acts are granted, not self-made: deeds foreordained by God and given inside the covenant (Eph 2:10; Rev 19:8 'given unto her'; Ezek 16:8-10)
Isaiah 64:6 explained as sin staining the deed's doer rather than obedience being filth
The bath/feet distinction (John 13): one baptism, ongoing cleansing of conduct
Nakedness as the antithesis: absence of righteous acts and covenant covering
The armor of God as God's own clothing of righteousness lent to the wearer (Isa 59:17; Eph 6:14)
strongest_counter_interpretation: The classic forensic/imputed reading: righteousness is fundamentally a right standing before God — Christ's righteousness credited to the believer through faith apart from works (Gen 15:6; Rom 4:3-8; Phil 3:9; 2 Cor 5:21). On this view Deut 6:25 describes an old-covenant arrangement superseded in Christ, 1 John 3:7 describes the evidence of righteousness rather than its identity, Rev 19:8 (per the KJV singular 'righteousness of saints') pictures the imputed robe, and Isa 64:6 shows that human deeds cannot constitute righteousness at all.
counter_core_identification: Righteousness is a legal/relational status declared and credited by God on the basis of faith in Christ, categorically distinct from and prior to any deeds; the believer's righteousness is Christ's, received rather than done.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that righteousness is identified with commandment-keeping done by the covenant member; it asserts righteousness is a verdict/status received apart from works, so the same term cannot centrally mean 'the doing of God's commandments' — the very thing the book's entry affirms and the phrase 'not a verdict only received' rejects.
counter_case: Genesis 15:6 — righteousness is counted to Abraham on believing, before any commanded deed is named
Romans 4:3-8 — God 'imputeth righteousness without works,' the strongest forensic proof-text
Philippians 3:9 — Paul renounces 'mine own righteousness, which is of the law' for righteousness through faith
Isaiah 64:6 — 'all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags' is read as disqualifying human deeds as righteousness
2 Corinthians 5:21 — believers 'become the righteousness of God in him,' suggesting conferred status
The KJV rendering of Rev 19:8 as 'the righteousness of saints' supports the robe-as-imputed-status picture
book_explanatory_advantages: Deut 6:25 and Ps 119:172 are explicit definitional statements equating righteousness with commandments observed — direct lexical evidence the counter must relativize as superseded
1 John 3:7 is an anti-deception warning whose whole force ('let no man deceive you') presupposes that a doing-less righteousness is the deception; the counter inverts its point
Rev 19:8's Greek dikaiomata is plural and active ('righteous acts,' so ASV/ESV/NASB/NIV), which the garment-of-deeds reading requires and the imputed-robe reading must suppress
The 'keep thy garments' texts (Rev 3:4; 16:15; Jude 23) only make sense if the garment is conduct that can be defiled and maintained — an imputed status cannot be soiled by the wearer's walk

Isa 64:6 is answered on its own terms: the verse says 'we are all as an unclean thing,' locating the filth in the sinner, not in obedience — the counter's proof-text is shown to cut against deed-hatred, not deed-identity
The book preserves grace: the linen 'was given,' deeds are foreordained (Eph 2:10), and robes are washed in the Lamb's blood — so it explains the gift-texts without denying the deed-texts
Job 29:14, Ezek 16:8-14, Isa 59:17, and the Eden coats-of-skins form a coherent cross-canon garment grammar (covenant covering + conduct clothing) that the counter leaves as disconnected metaphors

Accepted prior findings (faith as obedient trusting faithfulness; belief as submissive reception; love as commandment-keeping) make Gen 15:6 and Rom 4 harmonizable with the book's core without contradiction
counter_explanatory_advantages: Rom 4:3-8 and Phil 3:9 read most naturally, in isolation, as righteousness credited apart from works — the counter needs no harmonizing move there
Gen 15:6 attaches righteousness to believing, not to a named deed, at first reading
2 Cor 5:21's 'become the righteousness of God' is more directly at home in a conferred-status frame
The counter matches the dominant historical Protestant consensus, so it carries the burden of familiarity
decisive_sources: Deuteronomy 6:25 — Scripture's own definitional sentence: observed commandments 'shall be our righteousness'
Revelation 19:8 (Greek dikaiomata) — the wedding garment is expressly identified as the righteous acts of the saints, given yet done
1 John 3:7 — 'he that doeth righteousness is righteous,' framed as a warning against the contrary teaching
Revelation 3:4 and 16:15 with Zechariah 3:4 — garments that are kept, defiled, and washed require the garment to be conduct
Isaiah 64:6 read in full — the uncleanness is the doer's, defusing the counter's chief proof-text within the supplied bundle
unresolved_objections: The chapter does not directly exegete Romans 4:3-8 or Philippians 3:9; the harmonization of 'righteousness without works' with righteousness-as-commandment-keeping rests on the prior findings about faith and belief rather than on argument supplied here
How Genesis 15:6's crediting of righteousness to faith relates to the deed-identity is asserted via the faith premise rather than derived in this chapter

The precise relationship between the granted covering (justification-side texts like 2 Cor 5:21) and the woven garment of acts is sketched (covenant covering, then clothing of the covered) but not fully systematized
The KJV-vs-Greek rendering point at Rev 19:8, while lexically sound, is a translation-critical claim a reader must verify independently
